title: The segmentation clock needs a cell collective to oscillate and entrains grafted cells

fields.label: Label
fields.value: The segmentation clock needs a cell collective to oscillate and entrains grafted cells

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The vertebrate segmentation clock depends on collectivity: presomitic mesoderm cells do not oscillate when cultured individually but resume oscillating when cultured together, wild-type cells grafted into non-cycling mutant fish express her1 without cycling, and cells grafted into tissue at a different clock phase synchronize to their neighbours' phase.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: McMillen P 2024, Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates › Introduction › Segmentation intelligence is collective

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Similarly, pre-somitic mesoderm cells do not oscillate when cultured independently, but will resume oscillating when cultured collectively169.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: McMillen P, Levin M, “Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates”, Communications biology (2024), doi:10.1038/s42003-024-06037-4; section “Introduction › Segmentation intelligence is collective”. Scope: Vertebrate presomitic mesoderm (zebrafish, chick, mouse)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-collective-11: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The variables and decisive outcomes are clear. Published measurements likely permit checks of some components, but no known unified open dataset covers individual culture, mutant grafts and phase entrainment across the stated vertebrate scope.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare single-cell and collective presomitic-mesoderm oscillation traces, her1 dynamics in mutant hosts, and phase shifts after heterochronic grafting. The claim is supported if oscillation requires cell density and grafted cells converge on neighbour phase, and refuted by autonomous oscillation or persistent donor phase.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Single-cell movies and graft-level traces may exist only in supplements.

The three component experiments span species and laboratories.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.8
data adequacy: 0.6
operationalizability: 0.95
data existence: 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Independent mouse, zebrafish, and human pluripotent-stem-cell studies have published the collective-oscillation and entrainment results, so a restricted version of the claim can be checked by compiling those measurements. Raw fluorescence traces and graft coordinates are mostly supplementary movies rather than a public analysis-ready archive, and no single deposit covers zebrafish, chick, and mouse together. Harmonizing those sources is a months-long curation job, which is why this is only partly resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare Her/Hes reporter period and amplitude in presomitic mesoderm cultured as isolated cells versus as groups, and measure whether grafted cells adopt the host phase or keep their own. Loss of oscillation only in isolation, and phase-locking after grafting, would support the collective claim; persistent single-cell oscillation or failure to entrain would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Culture density, substrate mechanics, and Notch coupling can mimic a requirement for collectivity.

Chick and zebrafish are thinner in the published imaging record than mouse explants.

The dissociation, mutant-graft, and phase-entrainment results come from different labs and species and are not one downloadable time-series table.

fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.45
operationalizability: 0.85
data existence: 0.55
